descriptionChirho: Qal: to be hard, harsh, severe, or cruel in character or action, describing the quality of a person, situation, or treatment (e.g., harsh labor, fierce battle, cruel behavior).
Qal: to be difficult, hard to accomplish or understand, describing a task, situation, or matter that is beyond easy reach.
Hifil causative: to stiffen (the neck) or harden (the heart), expressing deliberate obstinacy, stubbornness, or spiritual rebellion against God or authority.

labelChirho: make difficult, ask a hard thing
descriptionChirho: Hifil causative: to make something difficult or to pose a hard request, as in asking for something extraordinarily challenging.
Piel/Hifil infinitive: to have hard labor, referring specifically to difficulty in childbirth (dystocia), used of Rachel and other women experiencing dangerous delivery.
Nifal: to be hard-pressed, oppressed, or in severe distress, describing a person suffering under difficult circumstances.
